correctness.rationale: PASS: The type (2,4) Humbert curve is a smooth genus-five complete intersection with tame (Z/2)^4 action. Each of the five character subsets of weight four gives an elliptic double-cover quotient; weight-two characters give rational curves. Prime-to-3 idempotents/isogeny split the Jacobian 3-divisible group into the five elliptic factors, preserving p-rank, a-number and slopes. In characteristic 3 the Legendre Hasse invariant is -(1+lambda), vanishing only at harmonic lambda=-1 (2=1/2=-1). A fixed triple of branch points has a unique harmonic fourth point, while any two of five four-subsets share three, so at most one supersingular factor: p-rank 4 or 5. The five equations a+1=b+1=a+b=1+a+b=a+b+ab=0 are smooth, disjoint after deleted diagonals, each is P1 minus four branch values; the simple Hasse zero gives reduced components. Counts (q-2)(q-3) total, 5(q-3) nonordinary and (q-3)(q-7) ordinary, with boundary q=3 empty. Independent finite-field arithmetic and projective cross-ratio checking verified q=9 and q=27 plus pairwise exclusion; finite counts corroborate rather than prove all q.
